text: dsh-rea-mcp 是一个面向 DSH 的 REA MCP 桥接插件，适用于需要让模型调用 REA 分析工具的场景。它通过 Cordis patch 插入 DSH 内置的 MCP 客户端，以 stdio 启动固定版本的 rea-agents，并将服务命名空间设为 rea。接入后，上游工具以 mcp__rea__<Tool> 名称提供给模型，可用于检查二进制、反编译和查询 REA 暴露的分析能力。工具调用超时为五分钟，服务器启动失败不会阻止其余 harness 功能。运行时需要 DSH 内置 MCP 客户端、PATH 中可用的 npx 和符合要求的 Node.js；首次启动会下载上游包。

dsh-rea-mcp connects DeepSeek Harness to REA analysis tools through its built-in MCP client. Its patch starts pinned rea-agents@6.4.0 over stdio and exposes tools under the rea namespace. Calls time out after five minutes. It requires npx and supported Node.js; first launch downloads the server.

怎么把 REA 的 MCP server 接到 DSH 上？
希望模型能使用 rea-agents 提供的工具。

I want my DSH agent to use REA analysis tools over MCP.
Connect a stdio MCP server for binary inspection to DeepSeek Harness.
dsh-rea-mcp 的功能「REA 工具接入」：通过 DSH 内置 MCP 客户端以 stdio 启动 rea-agents，并以 rea 命名空间向模型提供上游工具。
dsh-rea-mcp 的功能「固定版本服务」：桥接启动 rea-agents@6.4.0 的 mcp 子命令，避免版本随上游发布自动变化。
dsh-rea-mcp 的功能「启动与调用参数」：MCP 工具调用设五分钟超时；服务启动失败时不令整行 patch 激活失败。
dsh-rea-mcp 使用前须知：运行需要 DSH 内置 MCP bridge、PATH 中的 npx 和受支持的 Node.js；首次启动会由 npx 下载固定版本的 rea-agents。

dsh-rea-mcp README · dsh-rea-mcp：**A config-only bridge from [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) to [REA — Reverse Engineer Anything](https://github.com/morluto/rea).**

[中文](README.zh.md) · English

It mounts the MCP client bridge that ships inside DeepSeek Harness and points it at REA's MCP server over stdio. The whole integration is a single file, [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) — about 20 lines, no JavaScript, small enough to read in full before you install it.

dsh-rea-mcp README · dsh-rea-mcp：```text
DSH agent
  └─ mcp__rea__analyze_binary / search / decompile / ...
       └─ @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client        (ships with DSH)
            └─ npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0 mcp   (stdio child process)

dsh-rea-mcp README · dsh-rea-mcp：[REA](https://rea.tools/) connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, websites, network captures, Android APKs, firmware, SQLite snapshots and more. Analysis runs locally and returns evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. This bundle wires that into DeepSeek Harness as a plugin.

dsh-rea-mcp README · What it deliberately is not：- **No Host plugin.** No `index.js`; no code of ours ever runs inside your harness process.
- **No web route.** No new HTTP endpoint, so no new unauthenticated attack surface, and no reason to bind yet another path to loopback.
- **No state file.** Reads and writes nothing under `~/.dsh/...state.json`.
- **No installer that edits your profile.** `npm run prewarm` installs and verifies the upstream server in *your own terminal*; it never rewrites a profile patch.
- **No runtime dependency, no build step.** `dependencies` is empty; nothing to compile; no `allowBuilds` to grant.
- **No machine-specific absolute path.** The bridge resolves `npx` from PATH; this repository's test fails the build if any machine-related path leaks into a published file.
- **No `peerDependencies`.** The row merely *names* `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` and never imports it; DSH resolves its bundled copy from its own install, exactly like the official `templates/mcp` combo bundles. A peer would impose a hard activation gate whose prerelease SemVer rules silently reject legitimate hosts; the host range lives on `engines.dsh` for the market card instead.
- **No

dsh-rea-mcp README · What it deliberately is not：If you want an in-app dependency installer or a doctor tool, this ecosystem has plugins for that. This one trades them for "small enough to audit on one screen".

dsh-rea-mcp README · Prerequisites：- **A DeepSeek Harness that carries the in-box MCP client bridge** — declared range `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`; verified by the author on **0.2.0-rc.2** (desktop). The range is a declaration; the test is on that one build; the two are not the same thing.
- **Node.js on the PATH of the process that runs DSH.** `npx` launches `rea-agents`, which requires **Node 22.x (>=22.19), 24.x (>=24.11), or 26+** and npm. The author tested on Node 24.
- **Optional — a native analysis engine for deep binary work:** an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection need none.

dsh-rea-mcp README · Install：In-app: **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin**, paste one of:

```text
dsh-rea-mcp                                  # the npm package name
github:sheilacraig/dsh-rea-mcp               # the GitHub repository
```

For a CLI-held profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-rea-mcp
```

The Electron desktop's own `desktop` profile belongs to the app; use its plugin panel.

dsh-rea-mcp README · Install：**For local development, do not install a link that points at an external checkout.** To verify a local tree, pack it and install the tarball, which lands inside DSH's own plugin directory instead of leaving a link into your workspace:

```sh
cd dsh-rea-mcp
npm pack                          # produces dsh-rea-mcp-<version>.tgz

dsh-rea-mcp README · in the DSH plugin panel, Add plugin -> the local path of that tarball：```

Then **restart DSH** so the new patch layer is composed at startup.

dsh-rea-mcp README · First start is the slow one：`npx` downloads `rea-agents@6.4.0` and its dependencies on first use. On a slow link that is a while, and the harness gives up on the initial MCP connection long before that finishes. Cache it outside the harness first, where there is no timeout:

```sh
npm run prewarm
```
section: First start is the slow one

text: dsh-rea-mcp README · First start is the slow one：The script runs `npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0 mcp` — **the same argv the bridge runs** — speaks initialize + tools/list to it, prints the server identity, the latency and the full tool list, then exits. It launches the very process the bridge will launch, so success here means there is nothing left to download or discover on the harness side.
section: First start is the slow one

text: dsh-rea-mcp README · What the model can reach：Tools arrive named `mcp__rea__<Tool>`. The exact set is what upstream `rea-agents@6.4.0` publishes and can vary slightly by release, so this plugin does not claim a fixed count — run `npm run prewarm` to see the live list. Capabilities include:

dsh-rea-mcp README · What the model can reach：| Area | What REA returns |
| --- | --- |
| Native binaries | pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references |
| Go binaries | embedded compiler version, modules, replacements, build settings |
| WASM / EVM / firmware | sections, WAT forms, dispatch selectors, region extraction |
| JavaScript / Electron | modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC, native add-ons |
| .NET assemblies | metadata, CIL instructions, native dependencies, build comparisons |
| Android APKs / devices | manifests, decompiled methods, packages, processes, dumps |
| Websites | page structure, scripts, network observations, screenshots |
| SQLite / crashes / captures | tables, registers/signals, requests, exposed payloads, packets |

dsh-rea-mcp README · What the model can reach：Static JavaScript and .NET inspection read the supplied files without running the app. Runtime capture and device workflows run the selected target with **your user permissions**; consult each REA guide before enabling those.

dsh-rea-mcp README · Verification：1. Run `npm run prewarm` once — it verifies the server and the exact pinned version.
2. In DSH, ask the agent to call something read-only, e.g. `mcp__rea__inspect_go_binary` against a Go binary you own, or a static `.NET` inspection.
dsh-rea-mcp README · Security：This hands an agent the ability to read and analyze binaries on your machine, and (for native analysis) to drive an installed Hopper/Ghidra/IDA.

dsh-rea-mcp README · Security：- **stdio, not a listening port.** The bridge spawns a pipe-connected child; nothing binds a socket.
- **Least surprise by default.** `failOnStartupError: false` means a REA that cannot start logs the reason and leaves the rest of the harness working.
- **The harness file sandbox does not govern the child.** MCP tool calls are ordinary tool calls — approval policy can intercept them; the sandbox implementation lives in the harness's own file and shell tools, not here.
- **Investigate only what you own or are authorised to.** REA itself ships a responsible-use disclaimer; this bridge adds none of its own beyond that.
- **Pinned upstream.** `rea-agents@6.4.0` is fixed; an upstream release cannot silently change what this bridge does. Bump it deliberately, then re-run `npm run prewarm`.
- **Read [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) before installing.** That file *is* the plugin; everything else is metadata, docs, and tests.

dsh-rea-mcp README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Cause & fix |
| --- | --- |
| No `mcp__rea__*` tools | The bridge could not start the server. Run `npm run prewarm` in a terminal; it fails with the same reason. Most common cause: the process that runs DSH has no usable Node/npm on PATH (a desktop shortcut or editor can carry a different PATH than your terminal). The harness log has a `mcp-client(rea)` line. |
| Native analysis fails with "provider unavailable" | REA found no Hopper/Ghidra/IDA for that binary format. Static JavaScript and .NET analysis do not need one. Configure a provider per REA's installation guide, or raise `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` / `REA_HOPPER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` for large binaries. |
| Tools are missing after an upgrade | The tool set is what the pinned version publishes. Bumping the pin can rename or add tools; check `npm run prewarm` and your prompts. |
| A runtime-capture call exposes a file it should not | Those workflows run with your permissions. Scope what you point REA at; do not run them against sensitive targets. |

dsh-rea-mcp README · Development：```sh
npm install     # only devDependency: js-yaml, used by the test
npm test        # node --test — enforces this repository's claims
npm run prewarm # install and verify the upstream REA server
```

dsh-rea-mcp README · Development：`npm test` mechanically enforces: exactly one insert row pointing at `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`; `serverName` follows the tool-name namespace rule; the pinned `rea-agents@<x.y.z>` matches the prewarm script; `failOnStartupError` and the timeout are the documented values; the market entry obeys the curated-list submission rules; and no published file embeds an absolute path or drive letter.

dsh-rea-mcp README · Uninstall：Remove this bundle under **Settings → Plugins**, or delete the row from your profile patch. Uninstalling revokes the whole row. No residual files: the plugin writes nothing.
